newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-GOALKEEPER UNDERGOES SURGERY AFTER ATTACK BY FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GOALKEEPER UNDERGOES SURGERY AFTER ATTACK BY FANS.

text.p: A goalkeeper beaten up by fans following a Brazilian championship match at the weekend underwent surgery on Tuesday, doctors said.

Ricardo Pinto, who plays for Brazilian championship leaders Atletico Paranaense, needed a three-hour operation after a small clot developed on his brain, said doctors in the city of Curtiba, the club's home town.
They said Pinto was recovering well from the operation.
Pinto was injured following his team's 3-2 win away to bottom club Fluminense in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday. He suffered concussion and needed stitches in a head wound.

Dozens of Fluminense fans scaled the fences around the pitch after the final whistle and some attacked Pinto, who himself lashed out before being knocked to the ground. He was carried to the dressing room by Atletico officials.

Pinto, who spent nine years of his career at Fluminense, described the fans as "animals" in the dressing room afterwards. During the match Fluminense fans had insulted him and threw objects at him from behind the goal.
A Fluminense official said Pinto was to blame for the incident. "He provoked the fans. There is not a fence in the world that could contain an enraged multitude."
Pinto said after the game he had merely been celebrating when he made gestures which Fluminense fans interpreted as provocative.
Rio de Janeiro police questioned one youth in connection with the incident on Tuesday and said they wanted to interview two other men.
